hints.title: Separate relationships from tweets
hints.body: Keep a set of followees for each user. Separately, keep one global list of published tweets in publication order.

hints.title: Newest means scan backward
hints.body: A feed is collected by walking the global tweet list from newest to oldest and keeping tweets authored by the user or one of their followees.

hints.title: Stop after ten
hints.body: Because the global list is already in publication order, the first ten matching tweets found from the end are exactly the feed. Do not sort by tweet ID, which may not reflect publication order.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
followees = map from user to set of users
timeline = []          # pairs (author, tweetId)
feeds = []

for each command and its arguments:
    if post:
        timeline.push((user, tweet))
    elif follow:
        if follower != followee: add followee to followees[follower]
    elif unfollow:
        remove followee from followees[follower] if present
    else:  # feed
        visible = followees[user]
        result = []
        for (author, tweet) in timeline from newest to oldest:
            if author == user or author in visible:
                result.push(tweet)
                if result.length == 10: break
        feeds.push(result)
return feeds
```
